Title 3— The President
Executive Order 11876 •  September 2, 1975
Creating an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute Between the
Carriers Represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and
Certain of Their Employees
\  .; %
A  dispute exists between the carriers represented by the National 
Railway Labor Conference, designated in lists attached hereto and made 
a part hereof, and certain of their employees represented by the Railway 
Employes’ Department, AFL— C IO ; International Brotherhood of Boiler­
makers, Iron Ship Builders, Blacksmiths, Forgers & Helpers; Brotherhood 
Railway Carmen of United States and Canada; International Brother­
hood of Electrical Workers and the International Brotherhood of Fire­
men & Oilers;
This dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the provisions of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
This dispute, in the judgment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to a degree such 
as to deprive a section of the country of essential transportation service:
N O W , TH E R EFO R E, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), 
I hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate this dispute. N o member of the board shall be pecuniarily or 
otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any 
carrier.
The Board shall report its finding to the President with respect to the 
dispute within 30 days from the date of this Order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for 30 days after the board Has made its report to 
the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the
FEDERAL REGISTER, VOL, 40, NO.  171— WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 3, 1975

versions.research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 11876 (40 FR 40501, Federal Register of September 3, 1975; govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original), headed Creating an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute Between the Carriers Represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and Certain of Their Employees and signed September 2, 1975. It creates a board to investigate the dispute between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees represented by the Railway Employes’ Department, AFL-CIO and four named brotherhoods. Inventory: the order is a board order whose operative commands are 1 clause(s) as recorded in the dossier (whole). The list of parties attached to the order identifies the dispute and is not a separate command. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 11876 (the held text of the table prints the numbers and the subject lines in separate blocks, so the row is identified here by its number alone and the subject is taken from the order’s own heading). Owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C): the report date and the end of any statutory standstill are spent facts that do not end the order; they are not recorded as later events because no report text is among this packet’s citable evidence, so the claim states the functional spending without a date. The packet’s number-citation lookup over the held order texts (33,118 readable files) found no held text citing this order by number other than its own printings. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches were selected after reading their coverage notes (complete; no coverage warning; the USC edition runs through 2026-10-09 and the eCFR search to 2026-10-14, which cannot matter for an order whose end is shown in 1986 or earlier).

(2) The statutory standstill period is a spent fact, not an end. No other held order amends, supersedes or revokes this order before EO 12553, and the held-text citation lookup shows none. EO 12553 is the first held instrument that ends the order. The packet’s number-citation lookup over the held order texts (33,118 readable files) found no held text citing this order by number other than its own printings.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the establishment, report, standstill commands all serve one board investigation; none is shown to be an independent continuing command that survived the board’s functions, and none is claimed to have ended before the revocation.","savings_check":"Savings: The revocation has no savings clause and the order created only a temporary investigative board; no surviving appointment, transfer or right is shown, and a bounded search of the held 12553 text, the order’s own text and the OFR catalog shows no residual or continuing independent effect.","scope_check":"Scope: the dossier inventory was compared with the full held text of the order and matches its operative commands; the attached party lists are not commands. The order is a board order of its own and amends no other order."}
